questions.text:
Read the sentence given below to find out if it contains an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. if the sentence is error free, select No error or option 5. Ignore errors of punctuation if any.

Alex were (A) supposed to be (B) sterile, but they had (C) been wrong about that. (D) No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'A' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • Replace were with was.
  • We need a singular helping verb after a singular subject. 
  • Here, the subject is Alex ( a singular noun) so we need a singular helping verb(was).
  • Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.
     

The correct sentence is: Alex was supposed to be sterile, but they had been wrong about that.

Additional Information 

  • Helping verbs are verbs that help the main verb in a sentence by extending its meaning. They can also add detail to how time is conveyed in a sentence.
  • Auxiliary Verbs: Helping verbs that add meaning to the clause where they are being used are called auxiliary verbs.
    • To be: am, is, are, was, were, be, been
    • To have: have, has, had
    • To do: do, does, did
  • Modal Verbs: Helping verbs that perform other specific tasks to further modify the action or meaning of the main verb are called modal verbs. Modal verbs do not change form. They are:
    • can, could, may, might, will, would, etc.

questions.text:
Read the sentence given below to find out if it contains an error. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. if the sentence is error free, select No error or option 5. Ignore errors of punctuation if any.

Gunboats were (A) constructed so fastly (B) that they were (C) called "ninety-day gunboats" (D) No error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.Key Points

  • In the second part of the sentence, 'Constructed so fastly' is the mistake.
  • Generally, 'ly' is added to adjectives to form adverbs.
    • For Example- slow - slowly, quick - quickly.
  • Fast is both an adjective and an adverb, hence 'ly' is not required. It is not used in the English language.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option B.

Correct sentence: Gunboats were constructed so fast that they were called "ninety-day gunboats"

questions.text:
Directions: In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the button corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the ''No error'' option.

One of the best (A)/ way to improve your (B)/ memory is to practise (C)/ recalling information (D)/. No error /(E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the second part of the given sentence, the use of the singular form of the noun 'way' is incorrect.
  • The phrase ''one of'' in the given sentence is a singular term and is generally used to talk about a noun or a pronoun.
  • The noun or a pronoun used after the phrase ''one of'' is always in the plural form (as we are talking of one person/place/thing out of many).
  • Therefore, the plural form of the noun 'ways' should be used in place of the singular form 'way'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: One of the best ways to improve your memory is to practise recalling information.

Additional Information

  • The helping verb will always be in the singular form (here, is), as the helping verb agrees with ''one of'' and not with the plural noun in the sentence.

questions.text:
Direction: In the sentence below, identify the part with an error. Mark the corresponding option. If the sentence is error-free, opt for option 5, ‘No Error’.

She wants (A) / to go to (B) / a university but (C) / she don't have enough money. (D) / No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'D'.

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence is in part 'D'.
  • The word 'don't' is not grammatically correct in this context; the correct word is 'doesn't'.
  • When using third person singular nouns or pronouns (like 'she' in this case), we use 'doesn't' instead of 'don't' to agree with them.
  • The corrected sentence is: "She wants to go to a university but she doesn't have enough money."

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 Additional Information

  • 'Don't' and 'doesn't' are type of compound verbs known as contractions. While 'don't' is used for plural nouns and pronouns, 'doesn't' is used for singular ones.

questions.text:
Direction: In the sentence below, identify the part with an error. Mark the corresponding option. If the sentence is error-free, opt for option 5, ‘No Error’.

He went to (A) / the gym to (B) / try and lose (C) / some weight. (D) / No Error (E)

options.text: A
B
D
E

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'C'.

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence is in part 'C'.
  • 'Try and' is a common informal usage but not grammatically correct in formal language. The correct phrase is 'try to'.
  • The corrected sentence is: "He went to the gym to try to lose some weight."
  • The exact usage of 'try and' and 'try to' can often depend on regional dialects and levels of formality.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 Additional Information

  • Try to is generally more acceptable in formal writing. Try and is more commonly seen in informal, colloquial, and spoken English, especially in the UK.

questions.text:
Direction: In the sentence below, identify the part with an error. Mark the corresponding option. If the sentence is error-free, opt for option 5, ‘No Error’.

This mistake will (A) / be repeated unless (B) / we do not (C) / learn from it. (D) / No Error (E)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'C'.

 Key Points

  • The error in the sentence is in part 'C'.
  • The phrase 'we do not' is incorrect in this context. The correct phrase should be 'we learn'.
  • The use of 'unless' already implies a condition. Thus, it is unnecessary to use the negative 'do not'.
  • The corrected sentence is: "This mistake will be repeated unless we learn from it."

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

'Unless' is a conjunction that is akin to 'if not.' It establishes the idea of a condition being fulfilled.

questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement."

The mob killed the sub-divisional officer, didn't they?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'didn't it?'.
Key Points
  • Here in the given sentence, the wrong question tag has been used.
  • A collective noun takes a singular verb and singular pronoun in the question tag.
    • Example- The jury has taken its decision, hasn't it?
  • So, here in the given sentence collective noun mob has been used.
  • So, we need to use the singular pronoun in the question tag.
  • 'They' will be replaced by 'it'.
  • The sentence and question tag must be in the same tense.
  • The given sentence is in past tense so the question tag should be in the past tense.
The correct sentence: The mob killed the sub-divisional officer, didn't it?
​Additional Information
  • What is a question tag?
    • ​A question tag is a confirmatory question asked from the second person.

questions.text:
Direction: In the following question, two columns are given containing three phrases each. The phrases are labelled A, B, and C in the first column and P, Q, and R in the second column. A phrase from the first column may or may not connect with a phrase in the second column to make a grammatically and contextually meaningful sentence. Identify the correct option from those given below that gives the correct sequence in which one or more sentences can be formed. If none of the options makes it possible for a meaningful sentence to be formed, indicate 'None of these' as your answer.
 
Column 1 Column 2
(A) It is a beautiful morning  (P) today, isn't it?
(B) The match was postponed (Q) due to the rain.
(C) I want to go to the  (R) library tomorrow.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A-P and C-R.
Key Points
The correct combination of sentences among the given options is A-P and C-R.
Let us look at the sentence combinations in detail:
  • A can be used only with R to make a meaningful sentence: It is a beautiful morning today, isn't it?
  • A cannot be used with Q or R because it would not make a meaningful sentence.
    It is a beautiful morning due to the rain.
    It is a beautiful morning library tomorrow.
  • Next, B is used with P to make a meaningful sentence: The match was postponed due to the rain.
  • If B is combined with R, it does not make a meaningful sentence.
    The match was postponed library tomorrow.
  • Then, the last combination is C-R: I want to go to the library tomorrow.
The correct combinations will be: (A) It is a beautiful morning (P) today, isn't it? & (C) I want to go to the (R) library tomorrow.
 
​Thus, the correct combination of the sentence is: A-P and C-R.
Additional Information
A sentence may be grammatically correct but not logically correct.
  • Here, the sentence 'It is a beautiful morning due to the rain' is grammatically correct.
  • However, a rainy day is generally not considered a beautiful day.
Similarly, a sentence that might appear to be logically correct may be grammatically incorrect.
  • The combination B-P might appear to be a logical sentence:
    The match was postponed today, isn't it?
  • Here, the sentence is in the past tense in the first clause 'The match was postponed today', and the question tag is in the present tense.
  • Then, this cannot be a grammatically correct combination.

questions.text:
Direction: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.

Feasibility

A. The team conducted a feasibility study to assess the viability of the new project.

B. The feasibility of the new dessert in the menu depends on customer feedback and sales.

C. The feasibility in her argument was evident through her clear and logical reasoning.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the word given in the question:
  • Feasibility: the state or degree of being easily or conveniently done; the practicality or possibility of something. (संभाव्यता, व्यवहार्यता)
  • Now, let's examine the given sentences:
  • Sentence A: The team conducted a feasibility study to assess the viability of the new project.
    • This sentence correctly uses the word "feasibility" to describe the study of the practicality or viability of the new project.
  • Sentence B: The feasibility of the new dessert in the menu depends on customer feedback and sales.
    • This sentence also correctly uses the word "feasibility" to describe the practicality or viability of the new dessert based on customer feedback and sales.
  • Sentence C: The feasibility in her argument was evident through her clear and logical reasoning.
    • This sentence incorrectly uses the word "feasibility" because it doesn't fit the context of practicality or viability.
  • So, only Sentences A and B correctly use the word "feasibility" to illustrate different contexts of practicality or viability.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & B."

questions.text:
Direction: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.

Incentivise

A. The government decided to incentivise new businesses by offering tax breaks.

B. They wanted to incentivise employees for their hard work with bonus payments.

C. The school's policy was to incentivise good behaviour by allowing extra recess time.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the word given in the question:
  • Incentivise: to provide (someone) with an incentive for doing something. (प्रोत्साहित करना)
  • Now, let's examine the given sentences:
  • Sentence A: The government decided to incentivise new businesses by offering tax breaks.
    • This sentence correctly uses the word "incentivise" to describe the government's action of providing tax breaks to encourage new businesses.
  • Sentence B: They wanted to incentivise employees for their hard work with bonus payments.
    • This sentence also correctly uses the word "incentivise" to describe the action of providing bonus payments to encourage employees for their hard work.
  • Sentence C: The school's policy was to incentivise good behaviour by allowing extra recess time.
    • This sentence accurately uses the word "incentivise" to describe the policy of providing extra recess time to encourage good behaviour among students.
  • So, all three sentences correctly use the word "incentivise" to illustrate different contexts of providing incentives.

Therefore, the correct answer is "All A, B, and C."

questions.text:
Directions: Given below is a word, followed by three sentences that consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) that best express(es) the meaning of the word. Choose option 5 'None of the above' if the word is not suitable in any of the sentences.

SCRUTINY

A. The scrutiny folder inside the email will allow the user to delete all unsolicited mail in one click.

B. The teacher’s dull lecture failed to scrutiny any student interest.

C. Even though I wanted scrutiny, I decided to forgive my friend for her wrongdoing.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'None of the above.'

Key Points

  • The given word 'Scrutiny' means Critical observation or examination. (अति सावधानी से की गई जाँच; सूक्ष्‍म परीक्षण)
    • Example: The banks' activities have come under close scrutiny.
  • Let us explore the given sentences:
    • The word 'spam' should be used in the first sentence as it talks about the irrelevant or unwanted folder inside the email.
      • The word 'spam' means unwanted messages sent to somebody via email, especially advertisements. (ईमेल के माध्यम से भेजा गया अवांछित संदेश विशेषकर विज्ञापन)
    • The word 'provoke' should be used in the second sentence as it talks about the teacher’s dull lecture failing to evoke or arouse interest in any student.
      • The word 'provoke' means to cause a particular feeling or reaction. (विशेष भाव या प्रतिक्रिया उत्‍पन्‍न करना; उकसाना)
    • The word 'revenge' should be used in the third sentence as it talks about deciding to forgive or not take vengeance on a friend for her wrongdoing.
      • The word 'revenge' means something that you do to punish somebody who has hurt you, made you suffer, etc. (किसी से किसी बात का बदला, प्रतिशोध, चोट के बदले चोट)
  • Therefore, none of the above sentences expresses the meaning of the given word.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 5.

Sentence A: The spam folder inside the email will allow the user to delete all unsolicited mail in one click.

Sentence B: The teacher’s dull lecture failed to provoke any student interest.

Sentence C: Even though I wanted revenge, I decided to forgive my friend for her wrongdoing.

questions.text: What is the central theme of the passage, encompassing discussions about emerging technologies and their impact on society?

options.text: Recent transformations in the Indian IT sector
The intricate dynamics of cognitive warfare in the digital era
The potential benefits of AI adoption for corporate and governmental sectors
The complexities associated with transitioning to cloud-based infrastructure
The cascading effects of disinformation on government institutions

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points​To answer this question, let's first read the passage carefully to understand what the central theme of the passage is.

The passage discusses the impact of emerging technologies, particularly AI, on society, businesses, and governments. It highlights the challenges and threats posed by the rapid advancement of AI and the complex digital infrastructure it relies on. The passage delves into the concept of cognitive warfare, the manipulation of information, and the vulnerabilities in the digital landscape. It also emphasizes the potential consequences of digital uncertainty and the need to address the issue of "truth decay."

Now, let's look at all the given options:

  • Option 1 - Recent transformations in the Indian IT sector
    • This is not the central theme of the passage. While the passage mentions the IT industry in India, it is just one aspect of the broader discussion on AI's impact on society.
  • Option 2 - The intricate dynamics of cognitive warfare in the digital era
    • This is the central theme of the passage. The passage extensively discusses cognitive warfare, its techniques, and its implications, making it the primary focus.
  • Option 3 - The potential benefits of AI adoption for corporate and governmental sectors
    • This is mentioned in passing but is not the central theme. The passage mainly focuses on the challenges and threats associated with AI and digital uncertainty.
  • Option 4 - The complexities associated with transitioning to cloud-based infrastructure
    • While cloud-based infrastructure is mentioned as a part of the broader digital landscape, it is not the central theme of the passage.
  • Option 5 - The cascading effects of disinformation on government institutions
    • While disinformation and its effects are discussed, they are part of the larger theme of digital uncertainty and cognitive warfare. Therefore, this is not the central theme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2: "The intricate dynamics of cognitive warfare in the digital era."

 

Additional Information

  • ​How to find the central theme of a passage?
  • To find the central theme of a passage you need to first read the passage thoroughly and summarize it in your own words.
  • You need to find the idea that is being repeatedly focused on in the entire passage.
  • Look at how the passage starts and is wrapped up at the end to find the central theme of the passage.

questions.text: What is the primary focus of modern cognitive warfare, as mentioned in the passage?

options.text: Disrupting news media organizations and influencing public opinion
Altering human behaviour through sophisticated psychological techniques

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 5.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, refer to the following lines from the passage:
  • "Cognitive warfare puts a premium on sophisticated techniques that are aimed at destabilising institutions, especially governments, and manipulation, among other aspects, of the news media by powerful non-state actors. It entails the art of using technological tools to alter the cognition of human targets, who are often unaware of such attempts. The end result could be a loss of trust apart from breaches of confidentiality and loss of governance capabilities. Even more dangerous is that it could alter a population’s behaviour using sophisticated psychological techniques of __________."
  • From this information, we can conclude that the primary focus of modern cognitive warfare is altering human behaviour through sophisticated psychological techniques.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Altering human behaviour through sophisticated psychological techniques."

questions.text: What does the author mean by "truth decay" in the context of the passage?

options.text: A decrease in the accuracy of historical records
The physical deterioration of printed documents
A gradual erosion of public trust in official information
The decline in the quality of news reporting
The natural degradation of digital data over time

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

  • ​To answer this question, refer to the following lines from the passage:
  • "Today, government and government agencies are spending significant resources to undo the impact of misinformation and disinformation, but this may not be enough. There is not enough understanding of how the very nature of information is being manipulated and the extent to which AI drives many of these drastic transformations. All this contributes to what can only be referred to as ‘truth decay.’"
  • The author uses the term "truth decay" to describe the gradual erosion of public trust in official information. This erosion of trust is a result of the manipulation of information, the extent to which AI is driving transformations, and the impact of misinformation and disinformation.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is option 3: "A gradual erosion of public trust in official information."

questions.text:
Which of the following sentence(s) is/are false according to the given passage?

A. Government agencies are successfully countering the impact of misinformation and disinformation using significant resources.
B. The abuse of AI and emerging technologies has the potential to foster "truth decay," which can have far-reaching effects on governments, institutions, and societies.
C. By investing in intangible assets and moving operations to the Cloud, companies are fortifying themselves against AI-related threats.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

​​To answer this question, let's have a look at all the given sentences in the question:

  • Sentence A - Government agencies are successfully countering the impact of misinformation and disinformation using significant resources.
    • This sentence is false. The passage mentions that government and government agencies are spending significant resources to undo the impact of misinformation and disinformation, but it suggests that this may not be enough, indicating that they are facing challenges in countering these issues.
  • Sentence B - The abuse of AI and emerging technologies has the potential to foster "truth decay," which can have far-reaching effects on governments, institutions, and societies.
    • This sentence is true. The passage discusses the potential for AI and emerging technologies to contribute to "truth decay," which can have significant consequences on governments and institutions.
  • Sentence C - By investing in intangible assets and moving operations to the Cloud, companies are fortifying themselves against AI-related threats.
    • This sentence is false. The passage doesn't suggest that investing in intangible assets or moving operations to the Cloud fortifies companies against AI-related threats. Instead, it mentions that companies putting themselves at risk from AI and that the risks are increasing with the adoption of new technologies.

 

So, out of the three sentences, both sentences A and C are false according to the passage, while only sentence B is true.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & C."

questions.text:
Which of the following words will come in the blank taken from the passage?

Even more dangerous is that it could alter a population’s behaviour using sophisticated psychological techniques of __________.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

​​To answer this question, let's first understand the following line from the passage:

"Even more dangerous is that it could alter a population’s behaviour using sophisticated psychological techniques of __________."

  • In this context, the author discusses the potential consequences of cognitive warfare and how it could impact a population's behaviour through the use of advanced psychological techniques.

 

Now, let's understand the meanings of the given words as options:

  • Innovation - the introduction of new ideas, methods, or technologies (नई विचार, विधियाँ या प्रौद्योगिकियाँ)
    • For Example - 
    • The company's constant innovation in product design has made it a market leader.
  • Manipulation - the action of controlling or influencing someone or something cleverly or dishonestly (चालाकी)
    • For Example - 
    • He used manipulation to gain an unfair advantage in the negotiation.
  • Disintegration - the process of breaking down or falling apart (विघटन)
    • For Example - 
    • The disintegration of the old building was caused by years of neglect.
  • Elaboration - the act of adding more details or information to something (विस्तार)
    • For Example - 
    • The professor provided an elaboration on the key concepts discussed in the lecture.
  • Redundancy - the inclusion of unnecessary elements or repetition of the same information (अतिरिक्तता)
    • For Example - 
    • The redundancy in the report made it longer than necessary and harder to understand.

 

In the context of the passage, the word "manipulation" best fits in the blank because it conveys the idea that sophisticated psychological techniques are being used to control or influence a population's behaviour, which aligns with the author's discussion of cognitive warfare.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Manipulation."

questions.text: Which of the following words is opposite in meaning to "vulnerable" in the context of the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 4.

Key Points

To answer this question, let's understand the meaning of the word "vulnerable" in the context of the passage:

  • Vulnerable - susceptible to physical or emotional harm, attack, or damage; in need of special care, support, or protection (असुरक्षित)
    • For Example -
    • The old bridge was vulnerable to collapse due to its deteriorating condition.


Additional Information

  • Fragile - easily broken or damaged; delicate and not strong (नाजुक)
    • For Example -
    • The fragile glassware should be handled with care.
  • Transparent - allowing light to pass through so that objects can be seen clearly; easy to perceive or understand (पारदर्शी)
    • For Example -
    • The clear glass window was transparent, offering a view of the garden.
  • Elaborate - involving many careful details; intricate or complex (विस्तृत)
    • For Example -
    • The artist created an elaborate painting with intricate patterns.
  • Resilient - able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions; flexible and adaptable (प्रतिरोधक्षम्मतापूर्ण)
    • For Example -
    • Despite the challenges, the community showed a resilient spirit in rebuilding after the disaster.
  • Tenacious - tending to keep a firm hold of something; persistent and determined (दृढ़)
    • For Example -
    • She displayed tenacious dedication to her work, never giving up on her goals.

After understanding the meanings of all the given words, we can conclude that the word that is opposite in meaning to "vulnerable" in the context of the passage is "Resilient." Resilient means able to withstand difficult conditions, which is the opposite of being vulnerable.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Resilient."

questions.text: Which of the following words is similar in meaning to "exponential" in the context of the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

​To answer this question, let's understand the meaning of the word "exponential" in the context of the passage:

  • Exponential - growing or increasing at a very fast rate, often becoming larger and larger at a faster and faster rate (गुणोत्तर)
    • For Example -
    • The use of smartphones has led to an exponential increase in data consumption.

 

Now, let's consider the options:

  • Contrary - opposite in nature, direction, or meaning (विपरीत)
    • For Example -
    • Her actions were contrary to her words.
  • Tangible - perceptible by touch; capable of being touched or felt (स्पर्शणीय)
    • For Example -
    • The results of their hard work were tangible in the form of increased profits.
  • Rapid - happening or progressing quickly; with great speed (तेज)
    • For Example -
    • The company experienced rapid growth in the last year.
  • Consistent - unchanging in achievement or effect over a period of time (स्थिर)
    • For Example -
    • She maintained a consistent level of performance throughout the season.
  • Exasperating - extremely frustrating or irritating (उत्तेजक)
    • For Example -
    • The repeated technical issues with the software were exasperating for the users.

 

After understanding all the given words, we can conclude that the word "rapid" is the most similar in meaning to the word "exponential" in the context of the passage. Both words describe a fast and significant rate of growth or increase.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Rapid."

questions.text:
A sentence is given with four words marked as (A), (B), (C) and (D). These words may or may not be placed in their places. Four options with different arrangements of these words are given. Mark the option with the correct arrangement as the answer. If there is no change required, mark 'No rearrangement required' as your answer.

India continues to make every ensuring (A) in development (B) sustainable effort (C) and enjoyment of basic human rights for all its citizens (D).
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is CABD.

Key Points

  • Ensuring: making certain
  • Development: growth
  • Effort: attempt or try
  • Citizens: legally recognized subjects

Important Points

We may consider A, B, C and D to be four blanks. A is the first blank, B is the second, C is the third and D is the last.

  • One may make an effort. Therefore, the correct word for the first blank should be 'effort'.
  • A gerund is required for the second blank because the preposition 'in' is used before this. Thus the correct answer is 'ensuring'.
  • An appropriate noun should be chosen for the third blank because 'sustainable' is an adjective and it is used to qualify a noun. Thus, the correct answer should be 'development'.
  • The word 'citizens' is appropriate for the last blank because India is trying to ensure sustainable development for its citizens.


The correct sentence will be: India continues to make every effort in ensuring sustainable development and enjoyment of basic human rights for all its citizens.

questions.text:
Given below is a word, followed by three sentences which consist of that word. Identify the sentence(s) which best express(es) the meaning of the word. Choose option 5 ‘None of the above’ if the word is not suitable in any of the sentences.

MASSIVE

A. The gorilla had a massive forehead.
B. Eight massive stone pillars supported the roof.
C. The baby put his massive hand in mine.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '​Both A and B'.

Key Points

  •  The meaning of the word 'Massive' is 'large and heavy or solid'. It is an adjective.  
  • Sentence A has correctly used the given word. It is said that the gorilla had a huge forehead. 
  • Sentence B has correctly used the given word. The stone pillars must be huge and strong enough to support the roof. 
  • In sentence C, the word 'massive'  is incorrectly used. Babies are small in size. They cannot have huge hands. 
     

Additional Information

  • Synonyms of 'Massive' are- Huge, Enormous.
  • Antonyms of 'Massive' are- Tiny, Small.

questions.text: Which of the following is the FIRST sentence of the paragraph?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 5), i.e. T.

Key Points

  • The given passage is about the opinion of Indian professionals regarding future opportunities.
